terms.label: ACA₀
terms.scope: A stronger axiom system used in the wave reconstruction equivalence.

definitions.general: ACA stands for Arithmetical Comprehension Axiom. ACA₀ extends the starting rulebook RCA₀ with permission to collect numbers satisfying an arithmetic condition into a set, even when no general decision procedure is supplied.
definitions.physics: ACA stands for Arithmetical Comprehension Axiom. ACA₀ adds arithmetic comprehension to the base theory. In this wave problem it supplies missing tail-selection information needed to turn a rate-free Cauchy input into the required named limit.
definitions.mathematics: ACA stands for Arithmetical Comprehension Axiom. The extension of RCA₀ by comprehension for arithmetical formulas: number quantifiers are allowed, with set parameters, but no bound set variables. The wave statement WR is equivalent to this extension over RCA₀.
definitions.specialist: ACA stands for Arithmetical Comprehension Axiom. The exact strength of WR over RCA₀ for the declared rate-free representation. The upper bound selects Cauchy-tail witnesses; the lower bound recovers range existence through one scalar amplitude at t=0.

general.heading: Why an existence rule helps
general.text: An approximation sequence may eventually settle at every accuracy without telling you where it settles. The proof can use the stronger rulebook to collect enough information to specify a reliable limiting answer.

general.heading: What “equivalent” means
general.text: For this precisely stated mathematical problem, ACA₀ is enough to obtain the answer, and the ability to solve every allowed input is enough to recover the extra rule. Both directions are needed.

general.heading: What this does not mean
general.text: The result does not say that a laboratory needs an axiom system to function. Supplying an error schedule changes the mathematical input and avoids this extra requirement in the comparison.

general.heading: Names that must stay distinct
general.text: The subscript zero is part of this system’s name. Bare ACA can denote a different system, so this dictionary no longer automatically treats the two spellings as interchangeable.

physics.heading: Location of the extra assumption
physics.text: The upper-bound proof forms the condition that all approximants beyond N are close at a requested tolerance, then obtains witnesses for those tails. Propagation and detector integration are handled separately by explicit estimates.

physics.heading: Why the converse is interesting
physics.text: The detector can encode an arbitrary limiting scalar amplitude even at time zero. Recovering the requested output therefore cannot be justified solely by pointing to the simplicity of the wave dynamics.

physics.heading: Reading the result correctly
physics.text: This is a logical calibration of a representation and completion task. It is not a new physical interaction, a numerical complexity estimate, or a general obstruction to finite measurements.

physics.heading: Names that must stay distinct
physics.text: An ACA₀ requirement concerns existence for the specified rate-free input and fast output. It is neither a bound on laboratory resources nor an additional force acting on the wave.

mathematics.heading: Comprehension versus an algorithm
mathematics.text: Existence of a set defined by an arithmetical condition need not supply a computable procedure deciding membership. Number quantifiers can express noncomputable conditions even when the underlying data have effective codes.

mathematics.heading: Standard characterization used
mathematics.text: Over RCA₀, existence of ranges of injections characterizes ACA₀. The reduction encodes such a range in a limiting amplitude and decodes it from the fast output name.

mathematics.heading: Boundary of the comparison
mathematics.text: This does not assert all possible comprehension principles. The theorem names ACA₀ specifically and relies on the exact coding of its input promise and output function.

mathematics.heading: Names that must stay distinct
mathematics.text: The base and language determine the comparison: number quantifiers with set parameters are permitted in arithmetical comprehension. This is not comprehension over arbitrary predicates quantifying over sets.

specialist.heading: Upper and lower bounds
specialist.text: The tail predicate is arithmetical in the input code, so comprehension supplies a witness-selection construction. Conversely, a fixed profile and detector recover the amplitude code needed for range existence.

specialist.heading: Contribution and standard background
specialist.text: The scalar completeness reversal is standard. The project realizes it within its fixed detector benchmark and retains a supplied-rate comparison and exact finite reduction witnesses.

specialist.heading: No automatic promotion
specialist.text: The result is not a higher-type uniform operator theorem or a theorem about the full metric BV complex. Computational replay of finite witnesses does not certify the entire infinite reversal.

specialist.heading: Names that must stay distinct
specialist.text: The statement stays an equivalence over RCA₀ for WR. Retain the original coding, fixed detector and infinite-proof boundary when citing the result.

terms.label: Carrier
terms.scope: Project vocabulary for the mathematical setting supporting a construction; not a material medium.

definitions.general: The kind of mathematical structure in which a model is built. A finite collection of matrices, a space of waves, and an algebra of quantum quantities are different carriers, with different questions that must be checked.
definitions.physics: The specified mathematical realization carrying the model’s variables, operations and states: for example finite matrices, a completed function space or a local algebraic construction. Changing carrier may change which analytic obligations are meaningful.
definitions.mathematics: The chosen structured ambient object, including any topology, pairing, operator domains and completion data needed for a result. The matrix uses carrier as an organizational dimension rather than as one universally defined category.
definitions.specialist: The typed support of a construction in the atlas. Cross-carrier transfer requires a declared interface preserving the relevant operations and hypotheses; matching labels or finite fixtures do not establish equivalence.

general.heading: Why the choice matters
general.text: A finite table of numbers lets you perform exact finite calculations. A whole wave may require infinitely many approximations plus a rule explaining their limit. Both can model aspects of the same problem, but success with one does not automatically settle the other.

general.heading: Reading a matrix cell
general.text: The carrier tells you what mathematical objects that cell is discussing. The other dimensions ask what assumptions are allowed and which job—such as defining states or proving evolution—has been completed.

general.heading: Avoid a common confusion
general.text: This word does not mean the substance that carries a physical wave. It describes the mathematical setting used to investigate it.

general.heading: What a carrier comparison must preserve
general.text: Two models can use the same underlying numbers while measuring closeness or probability differently. Ask whether the proposed connection preserves the detector reading, not just the names of the variables.

physics.heading: Finite and continuum settings
physics.text: A finite mode truncation supplies matrices and finite sums. Passing to a completed field space can add convergence, domain, positivity and causal-support obligations. A successful truncation is evidence about that truncation unless a transfer theorem is given.

physics.heading: What to inspect
physics.text: Look for the space or algebra, the chosen topology, admissible states, domains of the dynamics, and maps connecting it to another realization. These determine whether two calculations address the same quantity.

physics.heading: Boundary
physics.text: The atlas tracks different carriers explicitly so their established results cannot silently be combined into an unproved complete theory.

physics.heading: What a carrier comparison must preserve
physics.text: A useful carrier change should specify the preserved dynamics, observables, pairing and causal support relevant to its intended use. Preservation of one property cannot stand for all of them.

mathematics.heading: More than an underlying set
mathematics.text: An identical vector space with two different topologies or pairings may support different continuity or positivity claims. A useful carrier specification therefore includes the structures used in the theorem.

mathematics.heading: Transfer question
mathematics.text: To carry a result to another realization, specify maps and prove the required compatibility—such as continuity, intertwining of differentials, or preservation of the pairing. The necessary conditions depend on the claimed result.

mathematics.heading: Project usage
mathematics.text: Carrier is an editorial organizing term here, not a claim that all entries form one category with interchangeable morphisms.

mathematics.heading: What a carrier comparison must preserve
mathematics.text: An isomorphism of vector spaces need not be a homeomorphism, a chain map or an isometry. Each extra preservation condition changes the interface statement.

specialist.heading: Interface obligations
specialist.text: State the source and target kinds and the exact property transported. A chain map, an SDR, a cyclic pairing identification and a causal operator identification answer different questions; one cannot substitute for the others.

specialist.heading: Why it matters to the programme
specialist.text: Reduced-mode certificates and local algebraic checks retain their dependency tags when compared with full Lorentzian targets. A positive finite test does not close the missing analytic transfer gates.

specialist.heading: Boundary
specialist.text: Read each interface certificate and its excluded claims. A coverage mark is neither a functorial construction nor proof of physical equivalence.

specialist.heading: What a carrier comparison must preserve
specialist.text: Finite-mode, Hilbert and local field-theoretic results require explicit joins. No full-import or causal-state claim follows solely from placing their certificates in neighboring atlas cells.

terms.label: Convergence rate (modulus)
terms.scope: Cauchy convergence in the wave input; “modulus” has other mathematical meanings.

definitions.general: An error schedule: for each requested accuracy, it tells you how far along an approximation sequence you must go so that all later approximations agree to that accuracy.
definitions.physics: A tolerance-to-index function controlling all later differences between input approximants in a specified norm. Supplying this function is stronger input information than promising that the sequence eventually settles.
definitions.mathematics: A function μ such that m,n≥μ(k) implies d(pₘ,pₙ)≤2⁻ᵏ. The Cauchy statement asserts existence of a suitable index for each k; a supplied modulus gives those indices as one input function.
definitions.specialist: An input function witnessing the ordinary-Cauchy promise in the exact second-order representation. WR omits it; WRμ includes it. This changes the completion obligation while preserving the detector and dynamics.

general.heading: A practical comparison
general.text: “The readings will eventually agree within one thousandth” gives you no stopping point. “From reading 500 onward, every pair differs by at most one thousandth” gives you one usable guarantee. A modulus provides such a guarantee for every requested accuracy.

general.heading: Why it matters here
general.text: A computer can produce better approximations without knowing when they are good enough. The wave comparison separates these two kinds of information: an eventual-agreement promise and a supplied error schedule.

general.heading: A limit on the analogy
general.text: These are mathematical guarantees for an ideal sequence. A few stable readings do not certify that every future reading will remain close.

general.heading: Use the schedule at the right interface
general.text: An error schedule is useful only when it describes the error you actually care about. A schedule for the input wave must be connected by an estimate to the detector’s output accuracy.

physics.heading: The norm is part of the claim
physics.text: A mode cutoff or numerical resolution is useful only together with an error bound in the topology required by the output. In this benchmark the input metric controls the smeared observable uniformly in time.

physics.heading: Using the supplied rate
physics.text: Given tolerance 2⁻ᵏ, select an input far enough along using μ, then spend the remaining error budget on interpolation of the detector response. The finite computations are unchanged when μ is supplied rather than obtained by a stronger existence principle.

physics.heading: Boundary
physics.text: A convergence modulus is not a physical frequency, a decay constant, or an empirical fit to a few errors. It certifies an entire tail of the specified approximation sequence.

physics.heading: Use the schedule at the right interface
physics.text: The detector continuity estimate transports input error control to output control. The supplied modulus provides tail information that the continuity estimate alone does not create.

mathematics.heading: Quantifier distinction
mathematics.text: The promise has form ∀k ∃N ∀m,n≥N d(pₘ,pₙ)≤2⁻ᵏ. It does not include a function collecting witnesses N. In a complete ambient space the tail estimate also bounds distance to the limit, but assuming that limit as already named would change the input problem.

mathematics.heading: An elementary example
mathematics.text: For pₙ=2⁻ⁿ in the rationals with the usual metric, μ(k)=k suffices: any two terms with indices at least k differ by at most 2⁻ᵏ. A general Cauchy promise does not present such a formula.

mathematics.heading: Related notions
mathematics.text: A modulus of continuity controls changes in the output as the argument changes. A convergence modulus controls the tail of a sequence. The wave output representation supplies continuity information separately.

mathematics.heading: Use the schedule at the right interface
mathematics.text: A modulus for a Cauchy sequence, a modulus of continuity and a bound on truncation error are different functions. Each must state its domain and the quantified condition it witnesses.

specialist.heading: Representation contract
specialist.text: The input consists of rational step-pair codes with a unit bound. Its ordinary-Cauchy promise is arithmetic in those codes. WRμ additionally supplies μ; replacing the input with an already completed state name would hide this extra information.

specialist.heading: Where the upper bound spends strength
specialist.text: ACA₀ forms the arithmetic tail predicate and collects suitable witnesses. With μ supplied, monotone majorization and finite interpolation suffice over RCA₀. The stronger principle is used for completion advice, not for the translation dynamics.

specialist.heading: Boundary
specialist.text: The equivalence concerns ∀ input ∃ output in second-order arithmetic. It is not an asserted uniform higher-type solution operator, nor a statement that every physically given source lacks a usable rate.

specialist.heading: Use the schedule at the right interface
specialist.text: Keep μ as an explicit part of WRμ’s input. A proof that a tail witness exists for each tolerance does not automatically supply the witness function used by the reconstruction algorithm.

terms.label: Observable
terms.scope: General concept with distinct classical, quantum and wave-example realizations.

definitions.general: A quantity a model connects to a possible measurement, such as position, energy, or an average wave amplitude. The observable tells us what we are asking about; the state supplies the information used to predict it.
definitions.physics: A specified quantity evaluated on a classical state, or represented by an appropriate operator or algebra element in quantum theory. Its mathematical definition and domain must be fixed before discussing predictions.
definitions.mathematics: A map extracting a quantity from a state, with the required structure depending on the model. In the wave example it is a bounded linear functional; quantum observables instead belong to an operator or algebraic framework.
definitions.specialist: The observable notion is carrier-dependent. The WR benchmark fixes a bounded linear detector functional on chiral energy data; it makes no identification with the full gauge-invariant Weyl observable algebra.

general.heading: How to think about it
general.text: A description of a wave contains much more information than one detector reports. To predict that report, the model needs a rule that turns the wave description into a number. That rule is the observable. Choosing a different rule asks a different measurement question.

general.heading: Example here
general.text: The wave example averages the wave over space, giving some locations more weight than others. Small errors in the wave data then produce controlled errors in this average. The project asks what information is needed to obtain a reliable limiting prediction.

general.heading: What it does not tell you
general.text: Predicting this average does not reconstruct the entire wave, and the mathematical averaging rule is not itself a calibrated laboratory instrument.

general.heading: From a number to a measurement claim
general.text: A number extracted from a formula becomes a proposed observable through a stated connection to a measurement. A detector profile is one part of that connection; calibration and noise assumptions are further parts.

physics.heading: Classical and quantum uses
physics.text: Classically an observable is often a function on phase space. Quantum mechanically a state supplies expectation values for observables; self-adjoint operators model real-valued sharp quantities, with domain conditions for unbounded operators. A specified expectation value is not an individual measurement outcome.

physics.heading: The wave calculation
physics.text: For chiral data p=(a,b), the fixed detector evaluates Oₚ(t)=∫₀¹h(x)[a(x−t)+b(x+t)]dx. The tent weight h is fixed rather than optimized with the input. The energy-norm bound controls the propagated error uniformly in time.

physics.heading: Why the distinction matters
physics.text: The reconstruction theorem concerns this functional and its coding. It does not by itself supply detector calibration, statistical noise modeling, or observables for the full metric BV theory.

physics.heading: From a number to a measurement claim
physics.text: The fixed smeared detector defines the wave benchmark’s output. This does not provide a complete operational identification for every observable in the full gravity theory.

mathematics.heading: Mathematical structure
mathematics.text: At each fixed time, Oₚ(t) is linear in the pair p. Its continuity is quantified by |Oₚ(t)−Oₚ′(t)|≤d(p,p′), where d is the stated L² product metric. This estimate lets finite input approximations control the output.

mathematics.heading: What must be represented
mathematics.text: WR requests a fast sequence of rational polygonal functions representing the time-dependent observable. Existence of an abstract value and existence of an output in this representation are different statements over a weak base.

mathematics.heading: Scope
mathematics.text: A bounded linear functional is the construction used here, not the definition of every observable in mathematics or physics. No full state reconstruction follows from this single functional.

mathematics.heading: From a number to a measurement claim
mathematics.text: An observable may be a scalar functional in a classical example or an element of a quantum algebra. Its representation, domain and continuity requirements depend on which object is meant.

specialist.heading: Exact role in WR
specialist.text: The detector and translated chiral data are fixed by the reconstruction source. The uniform operator bound factors error control through the input metric; interpolation produces the prescribed fast polygonal output.

specialist.heading: Lower-bound mechanism
specialist.text: On the fixed profile p(q)=(qg,0), evaluation at time zero recovers a nonzero rational multiple of q. Thus the reversal can encode scalar completion without using propagation or an unbounded family of detector modes.

specialist.heading: Claim boundary
specialist.text: Do not infer gauge invariance, a BRST observable algebra, a measurement model, or the accepted full-complex transfer from this reduced functional. Each requires its own construction.

specialist.heading: From a number to a measurement claim
specialist.text: The WR comparison preserves one observable across the two input representations. It does not certify a local algebra, a positive state on that algebra or renormalized products of its observables.

terms.label: RCA₀
terms.scope: A base axiom system for reverse mathematics; the old #rca link remains valid.

definitions.general: RCA stands for Recursive Comprehension Axiom. RCA₀ is the modest mathematical rulebook used as the starting point for this comparison. It lets the project distinguish what can already be proved from what needs an additional existence assumption.
definitions.physics: RCA stands for Recursive Comprehension Axiom. RCA₀ is a weak base theory for reasoning about coded numbers, sequences and countable mathematical objects. It is the bookkeeping framework for the wave comparison, not an extra law governing the wave.
definitions.mathematics: RCA stands for Recursive Comprehension Axiom. A subsystem of second-order arithmetic with elementary arithmetic, Σ⁰₁ induction and Δ⁰₁ comprehension, allowing set parameters. It serves as the base over which the stated reconstruction equivalence is proved.
definitions.specialist: RCA stands for Recursive Comprehension Axiom. The base for WR↔ACA₀ and WRμ. The input/output coding and all reductions must be available over RCA₀; importing an already completed input would invalidate the stated comparison.

general.heading: What a rulebook does
general.text: Mathematics starts with assumptions and asks what follows from them. Some familiar arguments use an assumption that an infinite object exists. Starting with fewer permissions makes it possible to see when that extra assumption enters.

general.heading: What happens in this project
general.text: If the wave data come with an error schedule, the project can prove the stated reconstruction within RCA₀. That is a claim about the proof and the information supplied, not about how intelligent a reader must be.

general.heading: Reading the notation
general.text: The small zero is part of the conventional name. You do not need to manipulate the formal axioms to follow the physical example; watch which objects the input already supplies.

general.heading: The role of the starting system
general.text: The subscript zero matters: RCA₀ names the particular starting system used here. It is not a grade of physical accuracy or a promise that every mathematical existence problem has an algorithm.

physics.heading: Why a physicist encounters it
physics.text: A derivation may pass from increasingly accurate finite data to a completed quantity. Reverse mathematics makes that step explicit. RCA₀ provides a restrained setting in which routine coded calculations can be separated from stronger completion assertions.

physics.heading: Application to the detector
physics.text: With μ supplied, one selects a sufficiently accurate rational step pair and interpolates its response. The report proves the required estimates in the base. Removing μ changes the existence problem, even though the wave equation is unchanged.

physics.heading: Avoid a misleading interpretation
physics.text: Calling this a weak base does not mean the physical model is inaccurate. Logical strength measures assumptions used in proofs, not experimental precision or runtime.

physics.heading: The role of the starting system
physics.text: RCA₀ supports the declared supplied-rate reconstruction because the error information is available as input. This does not assert that every arbitrary rate-free approximation can be converted into the same output within that base.

mathematics.heading: What second order means here
mathematics.text: The language has natural-number variables and variables for sets of natural numbers. Countable sequences and mathematical objects are encoded using these. The exact code for a real or a continuous function matters to the theorem being formalized.

mathematics.heading: Relative computability
mathematics.text: The comprehension scheme permits sets computable relative to available set parameters. It is misleading to conclude that every set appearing in every model of RCA₀ must be computable without parameters.

mathematics.heading: Use in a reversal
mathematics.text: To calibrate a theorem T over this base, prove the stronger system implies T and prove RCA₀ plus T recovers that system. A proof of only the first direction supplies an upper bound, not an equivalence.

mathematics.heading: The role of the starting system
mathematics.text: RCA₀ combines Δ⁰₁ comprehension with Σ⁰₁ induction and the standard elementary arithmetic axioms. Its role is relative to the second-order coding used in the theorem.

specialist.heading: Base-theory audit
specialist.text: Keep the ordinary-Cauchy promise separate from a selected tail witness function, completed energy input, or convergence oracle. The reduction must establish the required promise before invoking WR.

specialist.heading: What is certified
specialist.text: The report supplies an infinite mathematical argument and independent exact finite reduction checks. Those checks do not constitute a proof-assistant verification of RCA₀ formalizability.

specialist.heading: Scope of strength
specialist.text: The claim is an equivalence over the declared base and representation. A different output object or input name may have a different calibration; stronger ambient mathematics can conceal this distinction.

specialist.heading: The role of the starting system
specialist.text: PRA bounds for each fixed finite fixture and RCA₀ reconstruction results have different quantifier and representation scopes. Do not silently identify a family of finite certificates with the latter theorem.

terms.label: Reverse mathematics
terms.scope: Logical analysis of a precisely represented theorem over a stated base system.

definitions.general: A way of asking which mathematical assumptions a theorem really needs. First show that certain assumptions prove the theorem; then reason backwards from the theorem to see whether it recovers those assumptions.
definitions.physics: An analysis of the axiom strength of a mathematical assertion after its inputs, outputs and representations have been fixed. It can separate the cost of taking limits from the physical evolution being modeled.
definitions.mathematics: The study of implications and reversals over a specified base theory. An equivalence B⊢(T↔S) calibrates T against the additional principles S, with B held fixed.
definitions.specialist: An equivalence or implication analysis whose base, representation and quantifier form are part of the theorem. Here the focal comparison is RCA₀⊢WRμ versus RCA₀⊢(WR↔ACA₀).

general.heading: The backwards step
general.text: Ordinarily we begin with assumptions and prove a conclusion. The reverse step temporarily treats the conclusion as a rule we may use, then asks whether that rule lets us recover the original assumptions. This tests necessity as well as sufficiency.

general.heading: The wave example
general.text: The project compares two requests for the same detector prediction. One includes an error schedule; the other merely promises eventual agreement. The difference helps locate which information the proof needs.

general.heading: What is being compared
general.text: The comparison is between mathematical statements with specified inputs. It does not rank readers, and it does not decide which laws nature follows.

general.heading: How this fits the wider programme
general.text: Reverse mathematics asks which mathematical assumptions a precisely stated theorem needs. Reverse foundations of physics also asks about physical premises, mathematical settings and the connection to data.

physics.heading: Start with the physical question
physics.text: Fix the quantity to predict and what preparation data are supplied. Next specify how an approximation or limiting value is represented. Only then is there a definite assertion whose logical strength can be compared.

physics.heading: The informative separation
physics.text: In the wave benchmark the lower bound already occurs at one time and one profile. That locates the extra logical requirement in amplitude completion rather than in wave propagation.

physics.heading: Scope
physics.text: A sufficient set of axioms is only an upper bound. Proving that a particular algorithm fails is not a reversal: necessity requires a reduction from the target principle.

physics.heading: How this fits the wider programme
physics.text: A carrier comparison or empirical test can be valuable without proving a reverse-mathematical equivalence. Reserve the word reversal for an actual converse implication over the declared base.

mathematics.heading: Formal reading
mathematics.text: B is the background theory, T the represented theorem, and S the principle used for calibration. Both implications must be proved over B. Changing B or changing T’s coding can change the answer.

mathematics.heading: Example
mathematics.text: The rate-free wave statement asks for a fast polygonal name from an ordinary-Cauchy promise. Adding a function witnessing that promise yields a different statement and lowers the strength required in the report.

mathematics.heading: Distinction
mathematics.text: Reverse mathematics is related to computability theory, but axiom strength, effective uniform solvability and numerical complexity are separate questions.

mathematics.heading: How this fits the wider programme
mathematics.text: The target assertion includes its coding and quantifiers. A theorem about existence of a value and one about a named output can have different strength despite sharing an informal interpretation.

specialist.heading: Audit checklist
specialist.text: State the base, code spaces, promises, output representation, and whether the assertion is pointwise existence or uniform selection. Check that the reduction creates valid inputs without using the very comprehension principle it is meant to recover.

specialist.heading: Result here
specialist.text: The fixed-detector reduction realizes a standard scalar completion equivalence. Its scientific value lies in identifying the representation dependency of this benchmark, not in relabeling the background reversal as a new theorem.

specialist.heading: Boundary
specialist.text: No general claim about foundational necessity for physical reality follows from one represented mathematical model.

specialist.heading: How this fits the wider programme
specialist.text: The scalar completeness reversal used by WR is standard. The project’s claimed contribution is the controlled wave realization and supplied-rate comparison, not a new general classification of all field equations.

terms.label: State
terms.scope: Multiple related uses: classical configurations, quantum expectation rules and state cohomology are not interchangeable.

definitions.general: The mathematical information a model uses to make predictions about a system. What counts as a state depends on the model: a moving particle may need position and velocity, while a quantum model uses a different kind of description.
definitions.physics: A classical phase-space point or field initial datum, or a quantum density operator or normalized positive functional on an observable algebra. The carrier and positivity requirements must be stated; a cohomology class is not automatically a physical state.
definitions.mathematics: A model-dependent object on which predictions depend. Examples include a phase-space point and a normalized positive linear functional ω on a unital *-algebra, satisfying ω(A* A)≥0 and ω(1)=1.
definitions.specialist: Keep classical data, algebraic positive states, BRST state cohomology, and residual deformation classes separate. The existence or computation of one does not establish the others or an accepted full Lorentzian state construction.

general.heading: A familiar example
general.text: Knowing a ball’s position alone is not enough to predict where it will go next: its velocity also matters. A state supplies the information required by that particular model. It is a mathematical description, not necessarily everything one could know about the real object.

general.heading: Quantum use
general.text: A quantum state determines probabilities or averages for the measurements the model describes. It generally does not assign a definite pre-existing value to every quantity at once.

general.heading: Why this project is careful
general.text: Constructing a set of mathematical solutions does not by itself show that they give sensible probabilities. Entries in the matrix separate the underlying objects, existence of states, and positivity requirements.

general.heading: Keep three meanings separate
general.text: A wave’s initial condition, a quantum probability assignment and a cohomology class are different kinds of object. The word state should tell you which of these a passage means, rather than allowing one meaning to prove a claim about another.

physics.heading: Different realizations
physics.text: Finite-dimensional quantum mechanics can use a positive density matrix of trace one. Algebraic formulations define a state through expectation values, avoiding an assumed Hilbert-space realization at the outset. Field theories add analytic and domain requirements.

physics.heading: The relevant obstruction
physics.text: A negative expectation for A* A rules out a positive state on an algebra containing A. A finite-mode positivity construction does not establish positivity for the continuum or for a larger BRST complex.

physics.heading: Project boundary
physics.text: The residual classes [W₊²] and [W₋²] are deformation or vertex classes in this programme, not identified one-particle graviton states.

physics.heading: Keep three meanings separate
physics.text: A positive normalized algebraic state supplies expectation values. A vector in an indefinite gauge description or a residual deformation class does not automatically supply that functional.

mathematics.heading: Algebraic definition
mathematics.text: For a unital *-algebra, linearity, normalization and positivity specify the algebraic notion of state. Topological algebras may require continuity, and unbounded field realizations require attention to the common domain.

mathematics.heading: Cohomology is a different construction
mathematics.text: A quotient ker Q / im Q identifies closed vectors modulo exact vectors when Q²=0. Calling such a space state cohomology does not equip it with a positive functional or prove a probabilistic interpretation.

mathematics.heading: Read the carrier first
mathematics.text: When a matrix cell says state existence, inspect the underlying algebra or state space and the hypotheses. There is no single state set shared by every carrier.

mathematics.heading: Keep three meanings separate
mathematics.text: On a unital star algebra, positivity means ω(A* A)≥0 and normalization means ω(1)=1. A state-vector representation requires further structure connecting vectors and the algebra.

specialist.heading: Type discipline
specialist.text: Record whether the object is initial data, an algebraic functional, a density operator, a BRST class, or a residual vertex. Transport between these kinds needs explicit maps and compatible analytic structures.

specialist.heading: Reduced versus full
specialist.text: The reduced TT discussion concerns a specified commutator and positivity problem. Its conclusion neither supplies a full BV Hadamard state nor licenses identification of residual vertex classes with particle states.

specialist.heading: Current boundary
specialist.text: The current full serialized complex fails the export audit. A glossary definition is not evidence that the missing full state construction exists.

specialist.heading: Keep three meanings separate
specialist.text: The certified W₊² and W₋² residual classes remain centered deformation/vertex classes. Neither those classes nor a finite reduced positivity repair establishes the full metric BRST-compatible Hadamard state.

terms.label: Axiom and axiom system
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: An axiom is a rule accepted as a starting point for an argument. An axiom system is a collection of such rules. A theorem is a conclusion proved from them.
definitions.physics: An axiom system specifies the mathematical rules available to a model’s proofs. It is distinct from a physical postulate such as locality or a symmetry assumption.
definitions.mathematics: A theory consists of axioms in a specified formal language together with their deductive consequences. The language and underlying logic are part of the specification.
definitions.specialist: Axioms identify the deductive environment of a scoped result. In the atlas, logical principles must remain distinct from carrier structure and encoded physical premises.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Think of agreeing on the rules of a game before asking which moves are possible. In mathematics, a different rulebook can change which infinite objects can be proved to exist. This is separate from deciding which physical assumptions describe nature.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The same field equation can be studied with different existence principles. When comparing constructions, keep both the physical premises and the mathematical rulebook fixed unless the comparison explicitly changes one of them.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: In reverse mathematics the relevant theories concern numbers and sets of numbers. A statement’s provability is relative to a base theory; mathematical truth in an intended model and derivability in a formal system are different notions.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A claimed implication should expose which assumptions are discharged and which remain parameters. The atlas’s organizational notation is not evidence that every represented claim has been formalized in a proof assistant.

terms.label: Base theory
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A base theory is the shared mathematical starting point used to compare two claims. It tells us which reasoning is already allowed before asking what an extra assumption adds.
definitions.physics: The base theory fixes the mathematical resources allowed in a strength comparison. It plays a different role from a background spacetime or a reference physical model.
definitions.mathematics: A base theory is the formal theory over which an implication or equivalence is proved. Its coding conventions and induction and comprehension axioms affect the statement.
definitions.specialist: The base is a dependency of the reverse implication, not an informal label for an easy proof. Different finite fixtures and infinite assertions may legitimately use different bases.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: If both sides can already use ordinary finite calculations, those calculations are not the extra cost being measured. In the wave example, the question is what is additionally needed to reconstruct a limit when no error schedule is supplied.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The supplied-rate wave reconstruction is proved in RCA₀. Comparing it with the rate-free assertion measures additional existence assumptions under that base, rather than extra dynamics, experimental precision or computing time.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: To write T equivalent to ACA₀ over RCA₀ is to assert that RCA₀ proves the required directions. Changing the base can alter the strength comparison, so the base cannot be dropped from the theorem’s formulation.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The ladder’s fixed-fixture PRA claims and the wave reconstruction over RCA₀ must retain their quantifier and representation boundaries. A family of finite checks is not automatically a uniform theorem in the advertised base.

terms.label: Comprehension
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: Comprehension is a mathematical rule allowing a collection of numbers to exist as a set when membership is described by an allowed condition. Different systems allow different conditions.
definitions.physics: Comprehension specifies which sets of numerical information may be asserted to exist. In the wave comparison, it supplies information about convergence tails rather than changing the wave equation.
definitions.mathematics: A comprehension scheme asserts set existence for predicates in a specified syntactic class. Parameters and quantifier restrictions are essential to identifying the scheme.
definitions.specialist: Comprehension is the existence resource calibrated by the rate-free wave reversal. The relevant scheme is arithmetical comprehension over RCA₀, with the declared input and output representations.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For example, describing a collection is not always the same as giving a method that decides membership. The distinction matters when a proof collects information about infinitely many approximations to produce a limiting answer.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: An error schedule can provide useful tail information as input. Without that schedule, an existence proof may require a stronger comprehension principle. This is a statement about mathematical reconstruction, not a new physical interaction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: RCA₀ includes Δ⁰₁ comprehension; ACA₀ allows arithmetical comprehension. Arithmetical formulas may quantify over numbers and use set parameters, but do not quantify over sets. Arbitrary second-order comprehension is a stronger permission.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The upper bound and range-existence lower bound concern this scheme. Neither a numerical reconstruction routine nor finite witness replay establishes the full infinite implication, and no broader comprehension principle is inferred.

terms.label: Logical strength
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: Logical strength measures which mathematical assumptions are needed to prove a specified assertion. It does not measure how accurate a physical prediction is or how impressive an equation looks.
definitions.physics: Logical strength compares existence requirements for a fixed mathematical task. It is distinct from computational complexity, numerical conditioning and empirical adequacy.
definitions.mathematics: Relative strength is established through implications over a stated base. An upper bound supplies sufficient axioms; a reversal supplies a corresponding necessary principle.
definitions.specialist: Strength attaches to a formalized assertion or declared coding, not to a theory name, atlas color or carrier in isolation. The project’s reversal is scoped to WR over RCA₀.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Two tasks can use the same wave but provide different information about its approximations. The task with less information can require stronger existence rules to guarantee the requested answer for every permitted input.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The wave benchmark locates a strength difference in amplitude completion, with propagation and detector fixed. A stronger foundational requirement does not imply that a corresponding laboratory procedure is impossible or that the model fits data less well.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Equivalence over a base is stronger evidence than merely proving a theorem in a familiar system. Coding and quantifier choices belong to the assertion being calibrated, so changes of representation can change the result.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Do not promote a nonuniform existence result to a uniform operator theorem. Likewise, an analytic estimate and a logical upper bound constrain different objects even when both are described as bounds.

terms.label: Reverse implication
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A reverse implication shows that being able to solve the proposed problem would let us recover an assumption used to solve it. It is the direction that explains why an assumption is necessary.
definitions.physics: A reversal reduces a mathematical existence principle to the target reconstruction task. It identifies an unavoidable requirement of the stated task, rather than a failure of one numerical algorithm.
definitions.mathematics: Over a base B, the reverse implication T implies A shows that the target assertion T entails the principle A. Together with A implying T, it gives the stated equivalence.
definitions.specialist: The WR reversal uses scalar amplitude coding to recover range existence, hence ACA₀ over RCA₀. The fixed profile and detector locate the cost in completion rather than evolution.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Showing that a stronger rulebook can solve a problem proves sufficiency. Showing that any solution method for every allowed input yields that rulebook’s extra existence principle gives the converse comparison. Both directions have to use the stated common starting rules.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: For the wave benchmark, a scalar encoding can be recovered through a fixed detector at time zero. The lower bound therefore does not depend on difficult propagation or varying the physical apparatus across the reduction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The input encoding must be available in B, and the output must support the required decoding. An informal identification of limiting objects is insufficient if the theorem demands a particular name for that object.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The classical scalar reversal is standard background; the project’s contribution is its realization in the declared wave-observable benchmark. Exact finite checks support the encoding but do not replace the written infinite proof.

terms.label: Representation of data
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A representation is the form in which mathematical information is supplied. Two descriptions can refer to the same intended object while giving different help in finding an answer.
definitions.physics: A data representation specifies what an input code provides and what an output code must contain. It is distinct from the physical identity of the intended field or detector.
definitions.mathematics: A representation connects admissible codes or names with the objects they denote. Multiple names can denote one object, and representations can differ in the information their names supply.
definitions.specialist: Representation is part of the WR/WRμ specification. The observable and physical benchmark remain fixed while the input’s convergence information changes.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A sequence of approximations accompanied by an error schedule tells you when to stop for a requested accuracy. A promise that the sequence eventually settles does not tell you where. The project compares precisely this difference.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Supplying a convergence rate changes the reconstruction problem without changing the intended wave observable. Before comparing models or algorithms, check whether their interfaces deliver the same information, not just similarly named quantities.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The relevant theorem includes both input promises and the requested output representation. Existence of an abstract limit does not automatically supply a fast Cauchy name in the chosen base theory.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A representation-invariance claim needs explicit translations preserving the intended observable and the theorem’s available resources. Identifying two abstract carriers is not itself a resource-preserving translation of their names.

terms.label: Cauchy sequence
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A Cauchy sequence is a list whose later entries become arbitrarily close to one another. This describes how the list settles, even before a limiting object has been constructed.
definitions.physics: A sequence is Cauchy when its tail differences become arbitrarily small in the declared metric or norm. The relevant notion of error depends on the carrier.
definitions.mathematics: In a metric space, a sequence is Cauchy if for every positive ε there is N such that d(x_m,x_n) is below ε whenever m,n are at least N.
definitions.specialist: The rate-free input in WR carries a Cauchy promise without the schedule supplied in WRμ. The target still requires an appropriately fast name for the observable.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Approximations might eventually agree to a millionth, but the promise alone need not tell you which entry starts that level of agreement. A modulus supplies that missing schedule. Whether a limit belongs to the chosen space is a separate completeness question.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A field sequence may be Cauchy in one norm and fail in a stronger one. In the benchmark, distinguish the rate-free tail promise from a supplied bound on when each tolerance is met; the latter is additional input information.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Completeness asserts that such sequences converge within the space. A modulus chooses suitable N as a function of requested accuracy. In weak systems, the existence of those witnesses and a supplied witness function are different statements.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Keep the promise, the code and the output requirement explicit. A change from ordinary Cauchy data to a fast representation is not a harmless normalization when proving the reversal over RCA₀.

terms.label: Fast Cauchy name
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A fast Cauchy name describes a number or other object by approximations with an explicit, rapidly shrinking error rule. It tells a reader how much accuracy later entries guarantee.
definitions.physics: A fast name packages approximations with a prescribed accuracy schedule. It makes the detector output usable at requested tolerances without having to infer a convergence rate afterward.
definitions.mathematics: A fast Cauchy name is a coded approximation sequence satisfying a fixed effective Cauchy or limit-error bound, typically using powers of two. The exact convention belongs to the representation.
definitions.specialist: The requested fast output name enables the decoding used by the WR lower bound. Dropping that output requirement would change the assertion under study.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For instance, an agreed convention may make the error shrink by a factor of two at each stage. “Fast” describes this mathematical guarantee, not how quickly a computer produces the next entry.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: This is the output requirement in the wave reconstruction comparison. A physical observable having an abstract value is weaker information than an interface returning certified approximants to that value under the specified rules.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Equivalent standard conventions can be translated with index shifts or explicit estimates. Those translations should be stated when calibrating strength; an arbitrary rate-free Cauchy sequence is not already a fast name.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The rate-supplied upper comparison constructs the required output with explicit error control. Finite approximant checks verify pieces of this construction; they do not eliminate the infinite input promise or establish a uniform higher-type theorem.

terms.label: Completion
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: Completion enlarges a space so that its intended Cauchy approximation sequences have limits inside it. It makes precise a step often hidden in the phrase “take finer and finer approximations.”
definitions.physics: Completion passes from a preliminary space, such as finite mode combinations, to a space containing limits in a specified norm or topology. It is an additional construction, not a consequence of finite-mode success.
definitions.mathematics: A metric completion can be constructed from equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences, with sequences equivalent when their mutual distance tends to zero. The original space embeds densely.
definitions.specialist: Completion is a typed transition with both analytic and logical dependencies. The wave comparison isolates amplitude completion; the ladder distinguishes finite algebra, Cauchy, distributional and energy carriers.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: The rational numbers have sequences approaching numbers such as the square root of two, which is not rational. Completing the rationals adds their real limits. For fields, the chosen measure of closeness determines which limits are added.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A completed carrier may support operations or states that need separate continuity, domain and positivity proofs. The ladder records these additional obligations rather than treating exact finite energy as a full field-theory construction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: For normed spaces the completion extends the norm; an inner-product completion yields a Hilbert space. In weak foundations, distinguish constructing a coded completion from asserting limits for all rate-free sequences in a particular representation.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Do not transport finite identities into the completion without checking continuity or the relevant domains. The reduced positivity counterexample also demonstrates why separate finite repairs need not assemble into an admissible smooth full correction.

terms.label: Continuity
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: Continuity means that sufficiently small changes to an input produce small changes to an output, using the chosen meanings of “small.” It does not always tell us an explicit error schedule.
definitions.physics: Continuity expresses stability of a map under the topology chosen for its inputs and outputs. For a detector functional, it connects control of field approximations to control of measured values.
definitions.mathematics: A map is continuous when inverse images of open sets are open; metric formulations use ε–δ conditions. Uniform continuity and continuity at individual points are distinct assertions.
definitions.specialist: Continuity must be indexed by the actual carrier and target representation. The detector estimates in the benchmark do not supply missing tail information for a rate-free input.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A detector may respond gently to small changes in a wave measured in one norm. Changing how wave size is measured can change whether that statement holds. An explicit bound makes the dependence quantitatively usable.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A statement of continuity and a supplied estimate are different data. The wave reconstruction uses explicit bounds where needed; the rate-free amplitude problem cannot be solved merely by naming the detector continuous.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A modulus records a quantitative dependency between tolerances. Neither its existence in a chosen formal system nor its availability as an input follows just by writing a pointwise continuity hypothesis.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: When composing constructions, verify the topology and quantitative resources required at each interface. A continuous abstract map is not automatically a computable map between the declared codes, nor a uniform reconstruction operator.

terms.label: Topology
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A topology specifies what it means for points or functions to be close enough to count as nearby. It determines how we discuss continuous change and convergence.
definitions.physics: A topology determines the allowed limiting and continuity statements on a field or state space. Different choices capture different physical or analytic controls.
definitions.mathematics: A topology is a collection of open subsets satisfying the union and finite-intersection axioms. It defines continuity and closure; a metric is one way, but not the only way, to generate it.
definitions.specialist: Topology is a carrier dependency that must survive claimed transfers. Distinguish the structures used for finite algebraic data, completed modes, distributions and regular state corrections.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For waves, matching average energy is different from matching every derivative at every point. A sequence can settle under the first comparison and fail under the second. Naming the underlying set of waves therefore does not fully specify the setting.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Energy convergence, distributional convergence and smooth convergence impose different requirements. The cutoff example’s smooth correction requirement cannot be replaced by convergence of each finite block without an additional argument.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Infinite-dimensional spaces often carry several useful topologies. The same algebraic map can be continuous for one and discontinuous for another, so changing topology changes the relevant theorem rather than merely its notation.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A chain map or exact matrix identity supplies no topological estimate by itself. State precisely which convergence, density or continuity property is needed before passing to an infinite carrier.

terms.label: Vector space
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A vector space is a collection of objects that can be added and multiplied by numbers according to consistent rules. The objects can be arrows, lists of numbers or whole wave patterns.
definitions.physics: A vector space supplies linear combinations of configurations or perturbations over a stated scalar field. Linearized solution spaces often use this structure.
definitions.mathematics: A vector space over a field has addition and scalar multiplication satisfying the vector-space axioms. Finite-dimensional spaces admit finite bases; infinite-dimensional settings require care about the intended notion of basis.
definitions.specialist: Linear structure is one component of the carrier, not evidence for a compatible positive Hilbert realization. The project distinguishes finite exact mode spans from their completions.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: If two wave patterns belong to a linear space, their weighted sum also belongs to that space. This says how patterns combine; it does not specify distance, energy or probability, which require more structure.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The space itself does not fix a norm, pairing, topology or physical interpretation. In a nonlinear theory, adding two solutions need not give another solution, even though the ambient space of field variations is linear.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: An algebraic basis, a topological basis and an orthonormal expansion carry different requirements. Completing a finite-span space introduces analytic structure beyond its linear operations.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: When importing a complex, retain the scalar domain, grading and linear maps together with their claimed identities. An isomorphism of vector spaces need not preserve differential, pairing, support or state interpretation.

terms.label: Function space
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A function space is a chosen collection of functions, together with rules for comparing or combining them. It says which mathematical descriptions are allowed in a problem.
definitions.physics: A function space specifies the admissible fields, tests or initial data and their analytic controls. Smoothness, support, boundary conditions and integrability may each restrict it.
definitions.mathematics: A function space is a set of functions with declared additional structure, often a vector-space structure and a topology or norm. Membership conditions and the underlying domain are essential.
definitions.specialist: The ladder’s test and energy carriers discharge different obligations. Treat each space’s regularity, topology, support and domain conditions as dependencies of its claims.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Allowing every function, only smooth functions, or only functions with finite energy gives different collections. An equation can have a solution in one collection and not another, so “there is a solution” needs this setting attached.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Selecting a test space determines which detector functionals and distributions are meaningful. Selecting an energy space determines which estimates are relevant; neither choice should be inferred from the differential equation alone.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Spaces defined by integral norms may identify functions equal almost everywhere, while smooth test spaces retain pointwise representatives and support information. Transferring between these settings needs a specified map.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A finite Fourier construction does not itself establish a distributional completion or localized solution theory. The relevant embedding, density or extension theorem must be supplied before composing those stages.

terms.label: Norm
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A norm assigns a size to an object, generalizing the length of an arrow. It lets us express how large an error is and whether approximations are getting close.
definitions.physics: A norm measures field or state size and sets the error notion used by estimates. Different norms control different observables or derivatives.
definitions.mathematics: A norm is a nonnegative function with definiteness, absolute homogeneity and the triangle inequality. It induces a metric by the norm of a difference.
definitions.specialist: Norm choice fixes the meaning of the Cauchy and continuity hypotheses used at an interface. Norm estimates are analytic data beyond finite exact algebraic identities.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For a wave, one norm may emphasize total energy while another detects sharp local changes. Saying an error is small without naming the norm can therefore hide a meaningful difference.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A useful reconstruction bound should connect the input norm to detector error. An indefinite quadratic form is not a norm merely because it resembles an energy expression; a norm must be nonnegative and separate zero from nonzero vectors.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: An inner product induces a norm, but not every norm comes from an inner product. Completeness in the induced metric defines a Banach space; completeness with a positive inner product gives a Hilbert space.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The reduced positivity obstruction concerns a specified full regularity requirement, not arbitrary norm convergence. Retain the actual carrier and quantitative bounds when transporting a result or comparing finite approximations.

terms.label: Inner product and pairing
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A pairing turns two mathematical objects into a number. An inner product is a special pairing with positivity properties that support a notion of length and angle.
definitions.physics: A pairing can couple fields, dual variables or graded objects. A positive inner product provides the Hilbert-space geometry used for ordinary quantum probabilities.
definitions.mathematics: An inner product is a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form over the reals, or Hermitian sesquilinear form over the complexes. A general pairing may be degenerate, indefinite or between distinct spaces.
definitions.specialist: Pairing compatibility is an independent import and transfer obligation. Nilpotency and chain-map identities alone do not certify cyclicity, nondegeneracy or positive state interpretation.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: The familiar dot product of arrows is an example. Other pairings can return negative values for an object paired with itself, or pair different types of objects. Those may be useful, but cannot automatically be read as probabilities.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The full gauge description can carry an indefinite or graded pairing while a physical-state construction requires its own positivity test. Preservation of a differential does not guarantee preservation of that pairing.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The convention for which complex argument is linear should be fixed. Graded cyclic pairings introduce further signs and degree conditions; these do not follow from the ungraded inner-product axioms.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Keep the classical graded pairing distinct from a physical positive inner product. A residual vertex class and its pairing data are not thereby one-particle states with probabilistic norms.

terms.label: Hilbert space
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A Hilbert space is a space with an inner product in which every Cauchy sequence has a limit. It combines a way to measure length with a guarantee that appropriate approximations stay within the space.
definitions.physics: A Hilbert space is a complete positive inner-product space. It provides a familiar state-vector setting, but a physical model still needs operators, domains and a probability interpretation.
definitions.mathematics: A Hilbert space is an inner-product space complete in its induced norm. Its topology and completeness are part of the structure, not properties of an underlying vector space alone.
definitions.specialist: A Hilbert realization is one carrier choice in the atlas, not a universal destination already certified by the classical complex. Positivity and operator-domain conditions remain separate dependencies.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Quantum theory often uses such spaces for state vectors. Merely arranging finite wave modes into vectors does not construct the completed space or show that its vectors represent acceptable physical states.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Gauge variables may initially live in a larger indefinite setting. Passing to a positive physical Hilbert space requires a separate construction; reality of a spectrum or positivity at finite cutoff is not a substitute.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A completion of a pre-Hilbert space is defined relative to its positive inner product. In weak foundations, coding that completion and asserting existence of particular limits must be distinguished explicitly.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: When comparing a reduced mode construction with the full metric complex, retain the actual embedding and compatible state data. A formal cohomology identification does not establish the required Hilbert-space realization.

terms.label: Test function and smearing
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A test function describes how a detector weights different locations. Smearing means combining a field with that weighting to obtain an averaged quantity rather than demanding a value at one ideal point.
definitions.physics: Smearing pairs a field or distribution with an admissible test function to define a detector functional. Test regularity, support and normalization specify what the measurement idealization assumes.
definitions.mathematics: A distribution acts on a specified test-function space; smearing is this dual pairing. For an ordinary integrable field it may reduce to integrating its product with the test function.
definitions.specialist: The fixed detector is part of the WR benchmark and its reversal. Its profile, estimates and output representation must be held fixed when identifying the logical cost.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Imagine a microphone with a finite region of sensitivity. Its reading depends on both the incoming wave and its response profile. The wave benchmark fixes such a profile so the comparison changes the input information, not the detector.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The resulting observable can have explicit continuity bounds even when pointwise field evaluation is unsuitable. These bounds control detector error but do not themselves reconstruct an amplitude from rate-free approximation data.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Continuity is relative to the test-space topology. Compact support and smoothness are common conditions, not interchangeable with finite support of a coefficient sequence. The domain and allowed test class belong to the statement.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A smeared scalar observable does not supply a full local observable algebra, causal products or a state on the metric BV complex. Preserve that boundary when using the example to motivate the wider programme.

terms.label: Support and compact support
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: The support of a function is the region where it can be nonzero, including limiting boundary points. Compact support means this region lies in a compact part of its domain.
definitions.physics: Support controls where data, tests or responses can occur. Compact support of a source and causal support of its response impose distinct geometric restrictions.
definitions.mathematics: For a function, support is the closure of its nonzero set; for a distribution it is defined through where it vanishes on tests. Compact support means this closed support is compact.
definitions.specialist: Support preservation is a separate interface obligation in the ladder and causal construction. Exact finite residuals and nested Galerkin spaces do not establish it.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A detector profile can vanish outside a bounded region of ordinary space. A finite list of Fourier modes need not be localized that way: each mode may extend across the whole spatial domain. Two uses of “finite” are therefore different.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Finite mode truncation does not imply spatial localization. On a compact spatial domain, compactness alone also does not express confinement to a small region. The actual domain and support inclusion must be stated.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Support is a topological notion, whereas finite support of a sequence concerns its nonzero indices. Passing between coefficient and spacetime descriptions requires an argument; their supports cannot simply be identified.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A Green operator needs the appropriate advanced or retarded support property in the declared geometry. Do not infer that property from a formal inverse, a mode expansion or an algebraic chain map.

terms.label: Differential complex
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: A differential complex organizes objects and maps so that taking two successive steps gives zero. This rule makes it possible to distinguish meaningful structure from descriptions removed as redundant.
definitions.physics: A complex packages fields, gauge data or related variables with maps satisfying the appropriate square-zero identity. Its differential is not necessarily an ordinary spacetime derivative.
definitions.mathematics: A cochain complex consists of graded spaces Cⁿ and maps d:Cⁿ→Cⁿ⁺¹ with d∘d=0. A chain complex uses the opposite grading direction.
definitions.specialist: The current serialized full object fails its differential-square prerequisite. The trace/ghost candidate repairs exposed blocks but has not established full nilpotency and all compatible import data.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: If the two-step rule fails, the later classification called cohomology is not justified for that construction. The project’s current full export has such a consistency problem; fixing a few components does not establish the whole rule.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: This structure organizes redundancies, but its consistency does not by itself establish causal evolution or positive physical states. The full exported construction must pass its identities before claims depending on its transfer can be accepted.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The identity places images inside kernels, allowing cohomology or homology to be defined. An arbitrary sequence of maps, or a partially checked block matrix, is not yet a certified complex.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Keep a verified classical construction, a particular serialized export and a partial repair distinct. A scoped export failure blocks its dependent claims without automatically invalidating every classical or reduced calculation.

terms.label: Nilpotency
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: Nilpotency means that repeating an operation enough times gives zero. For the differential used here, the required condition is stronger and specific: applying it twice gives zero.
definitions.physics: For the BRST differential Q—named after Becchi, Rouet, Stora and Tyutin—the relevant condition is Q²=0. It is a gauge-complex consistency condition, distinct from solving the wave equation.
definitions.mathematics: An operator is nilpotent if some finite positive power vanishes. A differential is specifically square-zero, ensuring that its image lies inside its kernel.
definitions.specialist: Square-zero certification is an import gate, not a conclusion inferred from expected BRST structure. Nonzero Q² terms in the serialized export block the advertised full transfer.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: This is like checking that every two-step route in a bookkeeping system cancels exactly. A nonzero remainder signals an inconsistency in the object being checked, even if most individual components look correct.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The project’s current full export fails this prerequisite. A repair must establish the identity for the entire required object before dependent cohomology and transfer claims can be used; selected successful blocks are insufficient.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The distinction matters: generic nilpotency of higher order does not define the usual cohomology quotient with the same map. Exact arithmetic can test a finite encoded identity, but only for the supplied operator and domain.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Record the operator, domain and complete checked scope. The partial trace/ghost correction does not certify the repaired full complex, and a skipped check is not evidence of nilpotency.

terms.label: Cohomology
terms.scope: Mathematical background and its role in the reconstruction problem.

definitions.general: Cohomology records objects that satisfy a consistency rule after identifying changes counted as trivial by that rule. It helps separate surviving structure from removable descriptions.
definitions.physics: For a square-zero differential, cohomology is the closed sector modulo exact contributions. It can classify gauge-invariant information, deformations or anomalies, depending on the complex and degree.
definitions.mathematics: For a cochain complex, Hⁿ is ker(d:Cⁿ→Cⁿ⁺¹) modulo im(d:Cⁿ⁻¹→Cⁿ). The quotient is defined because d²=0 makes the image a subspace of the kernel.
definitions.specialist: The certified residual W₊² and W₋² classes are centered deformation/vertex classes. Local BRST cohomology, integrated functionals modulo boundary terms and residual state cohomology must remain separate result kinds.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A surviving class is a mathematical result, but its meaning depends on the problem. In this project, some certified classes describe deformations or interactions. Calling them particles would require additional physical arguments.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Local functionals, residual objects and physical state spaces are different targets. A nontrivial residual class does not by itself carry positive norm, a causal propagator or a one-particle interpretation.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
